newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: Malaysia warns Indonesian refugees to behave.
newsitem.headline: Malaysia warns Indonesian refugees to behave.

text.p: Malaysia has threatened to revoke the refugee status granted to Indonesian Acehnese if they cause trouble in the country, the national Bernama news agency reported on Wednesday.

"If the government finds that they are using this country as a base for their political activities, we will review their position and ask the United Nations to revoke their letter of approval (as refugees)," Malaysia's Deputy Home Minister Megat Junid Megat Ayob was quoted as saying.
Bernama said police detained 16 Indonesians in Kuala Lumpur on Wednesday for trespassing and demonstrating at the British, French, Dutch and Swedish embassies.
The men, believed to be illegal immigrants, were demanding political asylum and demonstrating against the deportation of 53 Acehnese, Bernama said.
Megat Junid was commenting on a riot at a Malaysian illegal immigrants' camp on Tuesday by the 53 Indonesians from the Aceh province of Sumatra who were protesting their deportation.
Megat Junid said the 53 were economic migrants who had turned political asylum-seekers when they knew they were to be deported.
He said several Acehnese in Malaysia granted refugee status by the government had turned up outside the camp to support the rioters.
Megat Junid warned that Indonesians could lose their permanent resident status and work permits in Malaysia if they became involved in demonstrations that could harm foreign relations.
"The government has treated Indonesian asylum-seekers well and they should not break the laws of the country," he said.

Hundreds of Acehnese have fled across the Malacca Strait separating Indonesia's Sumatra island and Malaysia since March 1992 to escape fighting between the Indonesian army and Aceh Merdeka, an Aceh pro-independence movement.
The United Nations has not recognised most of the escapees as refugees and Malaysia has said it will persuade them to return.
